title: I asked Claude to give my browser game's UI "motion graphics". The hard part was making the title load in without a single jump
author: Brave-History-6502
selftext:
Fjordfall is a quiet downhill skateboarding game set in Norwegian valleys, running in the browser (three.js). I build it with Claude Code. Today's brief was "use motion graphics, keep the UI minimal, make it fluid", and the clip is what came out.

  
What was interesting is where the jank actually came from. Claude filmed real frames with Chrome's screencast (about 56 fps) instead of trusting screenshots, and found:

  
\- A placeholder image that was swapped for the live 3D valley. Replaced with a plain CSS ground the valley fades up out of.

\- Fonts arriving late, so the words drew in a fallback face and jumped. The fonts are preloaded now, and the title's entrance waits for them (1.2 s at most).

\- A blur animation that froze mid-letter while the main thread was busy building the world. CSS filter animates on the main thread; opacity and transform keep going on the compositor. The letters now only fade and rise.

\- A 24 px layout jump when the game's code booted and set the page's "title screen" state. That state is in the HTML from the first paint now.

  
The menus used to open with motion and close in one frame, across about 56 different close paths. Rather than touch each one, a MutationObserver lays an inert copy of the closing sheet over the world before the next paint and lets it fade away. The real sheet is already closed, so input and focus never wait. The game's own UI checks caught three ways the copy confused them before it worked.

  
The selection cursor glides because gradients can't be transitioned but a registered CSS number (@property) can: fast in, slow out, so the row you leave keeps an afterglow.

  
Free, in the browser: [https://fjordfall.fly.dev/?via=ragd](https://fjordfall.fly.dev/?via=ragd)
